Based on the provided full text, the study meets several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5); uses reappraisal/distancing as the regulation strategy (Decrease) (I6); uses static visual images (IAPS pictures) as stimuli (I7); includes healthy adult participants (I8); and reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Neutral) (I9). However, the supplied article text does not provide peak coordinates for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps in a standard stereotactic space (Talairach or MNI) despite noting that “coordinates refer to MNI” and reporting FWE thresholds; numeric peak coordinates/tables are absent from the provided content. Inclusion criterion I10 (reporting whole-brain peak coordinates) is therefore not satisfied on the basis of the provided material. No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 are met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied, I must exclude this study from the meta-analysis on the basis of missing whole-brain peak coordinates in the provided full text (I10 not met).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed causal-attribution emotion regulation paradigm (reinterpretation-like reappraisal) with static visual stimuli (faces). The authors report within-task regulation contrasts ([increase+decrease] > view) and whole-brain group-level analyses with peak activations (tables) and Monte-Carlo correction. However, the sample includes both patients with lifetime major depression and healthy controls, and the provided full text reports combined/group-level results across patients and controls rather than presenting whole-brain activation maps or peak coordinates reported separately for the healthy control group. The meta-analysis requires that, in studies including clinical samples, results for the healthy control group be reported separately (I8). Because healthy-control-only whole-brain coordinates/contrasts are not clearly reported in the available full text, the study does not meet inclusion criterion I8. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered based on the provided content.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults who used cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion elicited by static IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulate vs view) and a group-level whole-brain GLM for the localizer with peak coordinates reported (see Table 2, Talairach coordinates). Methods, participants (healthy adult sample), stimuli (static IAPS pictures), task (reappraisal/regulate blocks), and whole-brain results are all present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., it is empirical, not ROI-only, includes whole-brain maps and peak coordinates). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables/Figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria listed below and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a reappraisal (distancing) strategy with static visual images (IAPS and photographs). The sample comprises healthy participants including adults (ages 6–23), participants aged 18+ are healthy adult subjects, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Reappraisal/Negative > Reactivity/Negative). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates are reported in tables and text (and supplementary material), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, clinical-only reporting) apply.

This is a task-based pharmaco-fMRI study in healthy adults that used an explicit reappraisal instruction (Think Objectively) to down-regulate responses to static IAPS images and reports reappraise>watch contrasts and peak activations for ROI clusters. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy used), I7 (static visual images - IAPS), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrast reported), I11 (results reported in tables/figures). However, the authors conducted ROI-constrained analyses (a priori L amygdala and R IFG; a frontal AAL mask for exploratory analyses) and report ROI/region-limited peak results rather than a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map reported across the entire brain. Therefore the study does not meet I10 and falls under exclusion E5 (reports only ROI/masked analyses without an accompanying whole-brain map). Full text appears complete. Exclusion ID(s): E5. Inclusion IDs met: I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I11. Inclusion ID not met: I10.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly implements reappraisal (self-focused reappraisal) to both up- and down-regulate emotion (I6). The regulated stimuli are static visual images (angry and neutral faces from the FACES database) (I7). The sample includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (HC n=22) so healthy results can be extracted (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., increase > view-angry, decrease > view-angry) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with standard-space localization and cluster-level FWE thresholds; results are presented in tables/figures (implying reported peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space) (I10,I11). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study that uses reappraisal (reduce emotion) to regulate responses to static negative images (IAPS). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately. Group-level within-task contrasts (Reappraise and Maintain versus Baseline; HC > anxious) are voxelwise whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates provided in Talairach space (Tables 2 and 3). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text (fulltext complete). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented a reappraisal condition (reappraise > attend negative) using static visual images from the IAPS. The sample includes a healthy control group, and the paper defines and runs whole-brain, group-level contrasts (reappraise > attend negative) and reports main task effects and group differences (with results stated to be in Supplementary Materials), satisfying the requirement that whole-brain peak coordinates are reported (acceptable in supplementary materials per eligibility rules). The methods describe whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholds (FWE cluster-level correction), indicating standard group-level whole-brain reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an explicit Reappraisal condition and reports within-task, group-level whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) with whole-brain analysis details and referenced coordinate tables/supplementary material. Participants are healthy adult meditators. However, the emotional stimuli are dynamic film/video clips (10–12 s film clips), not static visual images as required by I7. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during presentation of static visual images (IAPS). The sample comprised healthy younger and older adults with screening for neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Reappraise > Experience and Experience > Reappraise) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (Tables and figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly implements reappraisal (down-regulation) as an emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal vs view contrasts). Stimuli are static visual images (IAPS photographs). The paper reports within-task group-level contrasts related to reappraisal (reappraisal emotional vs view emotional) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak activations reported in tables (MNI space, SPM5). All inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are reported (not only ROI), task activation maps are provided (not only connectivity), and the sample consists of healthy adults with results reported for that group. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult women that implements a cognitive reappraisal-like strategy (LATER: consider long-term consequences) to down-regulate craving for palatable foods. Stimuli were static visual images (candy/dessert). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (LATER > NOW and OXT modulation) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implemented cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect (ERT using IAPS static images). The paper provides within-task contrasts for reappraisal (Reappraise > Look-Negative) at the group level and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (multiple peak coordinates and volumes are listed; FWE-corrected results are reported). The sample is a healthy adult group (n=49) with clinical exclusions. The stimuli for the reappraisal task are static visual images. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults using static IAPS images and reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts with coordinates. However, the key emotion regulation strategy tested is mindfulness-based 'Observe' (objective observation and labeling) and expressive suppression, not reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking with an explicit goal to change emotional meaning). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (reappraisal as the regulation strategy). 

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none ([]) 
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual images/IAPS), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported: Observe>Look, Suppress>Look), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps with peak coordinates), I11 (coordinates/tables/figures reported) 
(c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (reappraisal not implemented).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a reappraisal-style distancing strategy to down-regulate responses to static IAPS images, and it reports within-task regulation contrasts (CER vs NoCER) and ROI/PPI results (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the full text as provided does not report a group-level whole-brain task-activation map for the reappraisal contrast with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not satisfied). Instead, the paper focuses on seed-based PPI connectivity and ROI-extracted effects (ventral striatum ROI center reported) and relies on contrasts/seed definitions from a companion paper; no whole-brain peak coordinate tables for the regulation contrast are given. Therefore it falls under exclusion E6 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity and ROI-focused results without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I10. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal with static visual images and includes a healthy control group (I5, I6, I7, I8 satisfied), the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain, within-task regulation contrast (e.g., Reappraise > Look) with peak coordinates for the healthy control sample alone. The reported whole-brain coordinates are for a Group × Condition interaction and between-group comparisons, rather than a standalone healthy-group reappraisal activation map. Therefore inclusion criteria I9 and I10 are not met. This study effectively reports only between-group/interactions for the reported peaks, fitting exclusion criterion E7.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used as regulation), I8 (healthy adult control group included), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrast reported: REAPPRAISAL > NO REAPPRAISAL). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I7 (stimuli are 1.5s video clips of laughing faces, not static visual images), I10 (the key reported reappraisal effect was an ROI-based result in left DLPFC; whole-brain analysis yielded no significant task-activation peaks for the reappraisal contrast, so a qualifying group-level whole-brain task activation map with reported peak coordinates is not provided for the main activation finding). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) from the review list were directly triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet mandatory inclusion criteria I7 and I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly used cognitive reappraisal (Regulate vs Maintain) to down-regulate negative emotion (I5, I6). The regulated stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7). Participants were healthy young adults (normal-weight and excess-weight groups) with psychiatric/medical exclusions, so at least one healthy adult group is available (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Regulate/Maintain) (I9). Group-level SPM analyses and peak coordinates are reported (including MNI coordinates for insula seeds and between-group activation peaks), and whole-brain/PPI analyses were conducted (I10, I11). Full text sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present and complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply based on provided information. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

E4-E8: none met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal implemented), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates), I11 (coordinates reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 — stimuli are 15-sec film/video clips, not static visual images as required by the review objective, so the study does not qualify.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that directly compares reappraisal and acceptance using static sad images (IAPS and other pictures) and includes a healthy control group reported separately. It reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view) and whole-brain mixed-effects analyses. Thus I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. However, the provided full text does not include peak coordinates in a standard stereotaxic space (Talairach or MNI) in the excerpt (tables are referenced but numeric coordinates are not present here), so I cannot verify I10 (reported whole-brain peak coordinates). Because I10 is a required inclusion criterion and cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study must be excluded. Full text appears otherwise complete (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that directly compares cognitive reappraisal and placebo regulation. Reappraisal was explicitly implemented as a down-regulation strategy and practiced by participants. The regulated stimuli were static visual images (IAPS pictures). Participants were healthy adults, and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., RU–CUR, CUR–RU) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported in standard space (MNI/Talairach) in tables/figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal of static IAPS pictures and includes a healthy low-risk group, the paper does not report a within-group, whole-brain reappraisal contrast (e.g., reappraise>maintain) with peak coordinates specifically for the healthy control/low-risk sample. The manuscript reports main effects across all participants and between-group comparisons (high-risk vs low-risk), but does not provide a standalone group-level task activation map/peak coordinates for the healthy control group that could be entered into the meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criterion I9 (within-task contrast reported for the target healthy sample) is not met, so the study cannot be included. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I9. No exclusion criteria from the list are directly violated.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment using cognitive reappraisal (down-regulation) of negative IAPS images (static visual stimuli). The paper includes a separate group of combat-exposed controls (no PTSD) reported independently, satisfying the requirement for a healthy adult sample. The analysis contains within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures), in addition to ROI analyses. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (decrease) to regulate emotion (I6) while viewing static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample is healthy adults with exclusions for pathology and results reported for the healthy group (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-negative > look-negative) (I9) and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates/cluster locations in standard (MNI) space (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply: the study is empirical, includes whole-brain maps rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results, and reports within-subject regulation contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This study does not use reappraisal (or reinterpretation/distancing with an explicit regulation goal). It employs an approach–avoidance task probing emotional action control, not instructions to reappraise/ up- or down-regulate emotional responses; thus I6 is not met. It also does not report any within-task reappraisal contrast such as “reappraise > look” (I9 not met). It does meet several other inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I5), static visual stimuli (faces) (I7), healthy adult sample reported separately (police recruits) (I8), and reports whole-brain MNI peak coordinates for task effects (I10). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Therefore the study is ineligible for this meta-analysis because it lacks the required reappraisal manipulation and corresponding regulation contrasts.

Excluded because the regulated stimuli are dynamic video clips rather than static visual images (violates I7), and the sample consists of daily young-adult smokers meeting criteria for nicotine dependence rather than a healthy non-clinical adult sample (violates I8). The study does satisfy several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (uses distancing, a reappraisal-style strategy), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., close vs. far), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster results and peak coordinates reported in Table S1), and I11 (coordinates/results reported in supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that uses reappraisal of static IAPS pictures (decrease vs look) and reports voxel-wise analyses, but the primary sample consists of individuals with PTSD, not healthy adults. Although a separate healthy sample (N=14) was scanned with concurrent TMS-fMRI, those healthy participants did not perform the reappraisal task; thus no healthy adult task-based reappraisal activation results are reported. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy), I7 (static visual images), I9 (within-task regulation contrast reported), I10 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I11 (results/tables/supplement reporting noted). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I8 (no healthy adult group with task reappraisal results reported separately). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails I8.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults using static face images (Face Matching Task) and reports group-level whole-brain GLM results (coordinates in Supplementary Table S2). Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual stimuli), I8 (healthy adult sample), and reports whole-brain maps/coordinates (I10, I11). However, the study does NOT implement any emotion regulation (reappraisal) manipulation or instructions (the task is implicit face identity matching), so it fails I6 (reappraisal as regulation strategy). It also does not report any within-task emotion-regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look), so it fails I9. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Because key inclusion criteria I6 and I9 are not met, the study must be excluded.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implements instructed reappraisal and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain results, the emotional stimuli being regulated are social/monetary decision outcomes in the Ultimatum Game (i.e., offers and proposers' behavior), not static visual images. Inclusion criterion I7 explicitly excludes studies regulating monetary or social decision outcomes. Thus the study fails I7 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal ("decrease" instruction; reinterpretation/situation-focused reappraisal) to down-regulate emotion in response to static visual images (IAPS and matched photographs). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look negative, reappraise > distract) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates (e.g., amygdala and prefrontal peaks reported in MNI/Talairach-style coordinates and coordinate tables/figures). Participants were healthy adults (screened for psychiatric diagnoses). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The provided full text is limited to an abstract-level summary and does not include methods/results tables with peak coordinates. From the abstract, the study appears to be a task-based fMRI reappraisal study using static pictures in healthy adults and reports regulation contrasts, so I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 appear satisfied. However, I cannot verify that group-level whole-brain voxelwise peak coordinates are reported (I10). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm whole-brain coordinate reporting, so the study is excluded pending full-text verification.

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal (reappraising vs attending-negative) using static visual images from the IAPS. The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately and within-group and between-group contrasts are provided (e.g., reappraising > attending-negative). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and peak activations are reported in tables (Tables S1–S4 referenced), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain coordinates in standard space. The paper also reports GLM activation results and DCM effective connectivity, but the presence of whole-brain activation maps and coordinates means it is not excluded by connectivity-only criteria. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed cognitive reappraisal (I6) to down-regulate emotion; stimuli are static photographs of faces (NimStim) (I7); the sample is screened healthy adults with results reported for the control group (I8); the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise-Neg vs Maintain-Neg and others) (I9); analyses used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps normalized to MNI space with peak coordinates reported (Table 1 referenced) (I10), and results/coordinates are clearly described in text/tables (I11). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal with a healthy control group, but it does not meet the review’s core requirements: stimuli are dynamic video clips (not static images) violating I7, and the paper reports ROI-based network/connectivity analyses (DEPNA) rather than whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps with peak coordinates, violating I10 and matching exclusion criteria for ROI/connectivity-only results (E5, E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal task), I8 (healthy control group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli are videos, not static images), I9 (does not provide conventional within-task whole-brain activation contrasts reported for the healthy group in standard coordinate tables), I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates reported). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) in healthy adults (I8) that includes a cognitive reappraisal condition: the cognitive group was instructed to perform a ‘reality checking’ reappraisal-like strategy during negative/unknown trials (I6). The regulated stimuli are static visual IAPS pictures (I7). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing regulation trials to neutral/observe trials (exp ng > nt, exp uk > nt, per ng > nt) for the target sample (I9). They conducted group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and report peak coordinates (tables/figures) in standard space (Talairach), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, tables, discussion).

The full text is a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) with static visual images (IAPS). Participants are healthy adults and within-task regulation contrasts (increase > maintain; maintain > decrease) are reported. Whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses are presented with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and text). The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a reappraisal emotion-regulation paradigm (reappraise vs maintain) with static visual IAPS images. The sample includes a healthy control group (low-EXT) reported separately and within-group contrasts are provided (e.g., AR > AM). Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise with cluster-level thresholding and supplementary/online resources are cited (likely containing peak coordinates in MNI space). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study sample comprises only clinical patients (anxiety and depression) with no separate healthy control group, so I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately) is NOT met. Additionally, the study reports ROI-based analyses and PCA on ROI data and does not report a group-level whole-brain task activation map with peak coordinates, so I10 (whole-brain coordinates reported) is NOT met and E5 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain map) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy used), I7 (static visual images), I9 (within-task contrast ReappNeg > LookNeg reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis.

This full-text reports a 2-day task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants using cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) to regulate emotions elicited by static visual images (IAPS and internet pictures). It includes within-task contrasts (e.g., down-regulate vs look aversive; up-regulate vs look aversive; reappraisal vs distraction) at the group level. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain results) and provides peak coordinates in MNI space for several contrasts (e.g., vmPFC MNI 0,32,-20; right dlPFC 36,59,1; left vlPFC -60,14,7), and also describes ROI analyses. The target sample is healthy adults (female sample reported separately). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and coordinate tables referenced) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using self-focused reappraisal (distancing and increasing) with static visual IAPS images and reports whole-brain, peak-coordinate results, it involves a clinical sample (SAD) alongside healthy controls but does not report the healthy control group’s task activation maps/contrast coordinates separately in the main text. The paper reports combined (across-group) activation for regulation contrasts and between-group comparisons, but I cannot find group-level whole-brain coordinates presented for the healthy control group alone for the regulation contrasts of interest (DistA > PermA, IncA > PermA). Therefore it does not meet the requirement that results for the healthy control group be reported separately, so the study cannot supply the healthy-only whole-brain reappraisal coordinates needed for the meta-analysis.

This full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) in which healthy adult participants used cognitive reappraisal (increase, maintain, decrease) to regulate emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Increase vs Maintain, Decrease vs Maintain), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and peak coordinates in standard MNI space (tables and figures; FWE-corrected results reported). The sample is healthy adults with exclusions for psychiatric/neurological illness. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly used cognitive reappraisal (self-distancing) as the regulation strategy (I6). The regulated stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample consisted of healthy adult participants (young females) with exclusions applied for motion and poor performance; healthy control data are reported (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts comparing Distance (reappraise) and Attend conditions (e.g., Response: Attend>Distance; Prediction Error: Distance>Attend) (I9). Analyses were whole-brain, normalized to MNI space, cluster-FWE corrected, and peak coordinates are reported (e.g., MNI coordinates reported for PPI and referenced tables S2 of activations), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given these points, the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and should be included.

This study does not meet the key reappraisal criterion (I6). Although it is a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants (I5, I8) using static visual images (fearful faces) as stimuli (I7), and it reports within-task block contrasts related to induced emotion/regulation demand (I9), participants were not instructed to use reappraisal (reinterpretation, distancing, or perspective-taking) — the paradigm induced mood implicitly via point gain/loss and assessed resulting brain responses. Therefore I6 is not met. In addition, the reported full text does not present whole-brain peak coordinates in standard space for an explicit regulation contrast (I10 not met based on provided text). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) appear to be directly triggered by the provided full text.

This is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (explicit 'decrease' instructions) to down-regulate negative emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS and child picture set). The sample includes healthy young adults (18–22) alongside children/adolescents. The paper reports within-task contrasts for regulation (decrease negative > look negative) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported in Talairach space (see main text and supplementary tables). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=58) using instruction-induced reappraisal (reinterpretation) to down-regulate emotion in response to static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Reappraise > Attend; Attend > Reappraise) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space (prefrontal, amygdala coordinates cited). All core sections (methods, results, discussion) are present. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for task, strategy, stimulus type, healthy sample, regulation contrasts, and whole-brain coordinate reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) to regulate emotions elicited by static visual images (IAPS). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=23) with no neurological/psychiatric history. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative) from a whole-brain GLM transformed into Talairach space and provides peak coordinates for ROIs (e.g., left IFG: −45,26,7) and whole-brain thresholding/cluster results (figures/tables referenced). Although PPI connectivity analyses are included, univariate whole-brain task activation maps are reported, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise group-level maps with coordinates. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation using static IAPS images and a reappraisal-like instruction (‘‘diminish’’ = imagine a less-negative outcome). It includes a healthy control group. However, the paper’s reported results and the provided full text focus on between-group comparisons (PTSD vs. controls) rather than reporting within-sample (healthy-controls) whole-brain regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise>maintain) or presenting peak coordinates for such whole-brain maps. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E7 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no clear within-task/regulation contrast reported for the healthy control group in the provided text) and I10 (no peak coordinates for whole-brain group-level maps for the healthy sample are present in the provided full text).

This is a task fMRI study in healthy adults that uses a cognitive reappraisal-like strategy (‘reality checking’) and reports whole-brain, group-level coordinates. However it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: the instructed regulation was applied during the anticipation period (cues) rather than to the static visual images themselves—i.e. the regulated stimuli are anticipatory cues/anticipatory state rather than the static pictures (violates I7). Further, the manipulation is implemented as a between-subjects strategy comparison (cognitive-control group vs basic group) rather than a within-task regulation contrast such as reappraise > look or down-regulate > maintain within the same participants, so there is no explicit within-task regulation contrast isolating reappraisal (violates I9). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal-like strategy used), I8 (healthy adult sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 are directly met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults (n=30) using a standard cognitive reappraisal paradigm to down-regulate negative emotion elicited by static visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reapp Neg vs Look Neg), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports peak coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures and cluster peaks described). Participants were healthy and results for the healthy sample are presented. No exclusion criteria are met (the study includes whole-brain maps and is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not a review, and not a between-group-only report). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly uses cognitive reappraisal instructions to downregulate negative affect (I6) while participants view static IAPS images (I7). A healthy control group is reported separately alongside a clinical group, enabling extraction of healthy adult results (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain; I9). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistics with multiple-comparison correction, and MNI peak coordinates are reported for key seeds/ROIs and connectivity clusters, consistent with I10; whole-brain task effects are described and results are presented in text/tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (none of E4–E8 apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented an emotion regulation task including a reappraise instruction (Sad-Reappraise vs Sad-View). The regulated stimuli were static sad images (visual photographs). Participants were adult females screened with SCID and without MDD (non-clinical/subclinical sample), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View) and describes group-level voxelwise GLM analyses with normalization to MNI space and cluster tables referenced in the results (whole-brain maps and peak Z values reported). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not incomplete). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly implements a cognitive reappraisal instruction (REAP: “pretend unreal”) to down-regulate emotion (I6). Stimuli are static visual images (IAPS and internet photographs) presented during the task (I7). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (female; no psychiatric/neurological history) (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation conditions (e.g., REAP > ESUP, REAP vs NAT) (I9). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps with reported peak coordinates in MNI space and tables of activations (I10,I11). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided and complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is excluded because the emotional stimuli regulated are anticipatory cues and delivered pain (electrical stimulation), not static visual images. Inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli = static visual images) is not met. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used as regulation), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with coordinates), and I11 (results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implemented an incidental/implicit cognitive reappraisal manipulation (non-negative vs negative preceding descriptions) to down-regulate emotional responses to static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (NNEG-DESC > NEG-DESC), voxel-wise whole-brain group analyses with cluster correction, and tables/figures listing peak coordinates in standard space (Talairach/MNI). Participants were screened healthy adults and results for this group are reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of eligibility.

This study meets multiple inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), implements reappraisal as an explicit regulation condition (REAP) (I6), uses static visual images (I7), tests healthy adult participants (I8), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I10) (coordinates for multiple clusters are provided in the text) and figures/tables (I11). However, the paper does not report a clear within-task emotion-regulation contrast of the form required by the review (e.g., reappraise > look, down-regulate > maintain) at the group whole-brain level in this manuscript. The authors state that main effects of regulation strategies are described in a separate report, and the present article reports parametric/modulation analyses (social vs nonsocial within each viewing condition) and correlations with attachment measures rather than an explicit REAP > NAT (or equivalent) contrast suitable for inclusion per I9. Therefore I exclude this article because it does not meet inclusion criterion I9 (within-task regulation contrast reported here).

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: the study is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that explicitly uses cognitive reappraisal/reinterpretation to down-regulate negative emotion (I6). Stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (undergraduate students) screened for neurological/psychiatric history; results for the healthy groups are reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise > Negative and Negative > Reappraise) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported with FDR correction and peak coordinates given in MNI space (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical limitations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. This study is excluded because it does not meet the reappraisal and stimulus-type criteria required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based functional MRI using continuous arterial spin labelling during an active task), I8 (healthy adult sample with separate group reported), I9 (within-task contrasts relating to regulation manipulation: instructed vs spontaneous and emotional vs neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates reported), and I11 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (does NOT implement reappraisal; the regulation manipulation is spontaneous avoidance vs an instruction to avoid negative sentences, which is not reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing as defined), I7 (stimuli are written scrambled sentences/words, not static visual images such as IAPS pictures or photographs). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Because two required inclusion criteria (I6 and I7) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain coordinates (see Methods, Results, and Table 2), the emotion regulation manipulation is an imagery-focused strategy (instructing participants to imagine a calming or exciting scene) rather than reappraisal (e.g., reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing). The review’s reappraisal criterion (I6) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual CS images used), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak coordinates), I11 (coordinates reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal as defined by the review (I6 not met).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that implements cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate craving (I6); regulated stimuli are static visual food images (I7); participants are healthy adults with exclusions for neurological/psychiatric disorders and results are reported for this group (I8); the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Regulate > Look, RC > LC) (I9); analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, and peak coordinates are reported in MNI space (I10); whole-brain results and coordinates are clearly described in text/tables (I11). Full article includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply. Given these points, the study should be included for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy older adults using reappraisal (reinterpretation/distancing) of static visual images (IAPS) and reports within-task regulation contrasts. However, the fMRI results were analyzed and reported using an ROI approach (predefined ROIs) and the paper does not present group-level whole-brain, voxelwise activation maps with reported peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only ROI analyses without an accompanying whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy), I7 (static visual images), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults using reappraisal to down-regulate emotions elicited by static visual images (I5, I6, I7, I8) and it reports within-task contrasts for regulation (reappraisal vs. watching) used in ROI analyses (I9), the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map with peak coordinates for the reappraisal/regulation contrasts. The main regulation results are presented via amygdala small-volume correction/ROI percent-signal-change and ROI-based statistics rather than whole-brain peak coordinates. Therefore it fails the whole-brain coordinates requirement (I10) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI/SVC-only results without accompanying whole-brain map).

This paper is a task-based fMRI study using an established reappraisal paradigm (increase/decrease instructions) with static visual images from the IAPS. It reports within-task contrasts (negative decrease > attend) and presents voxel-wise, whole-brain mixed-effects GLM results with Talairach coordinates and cluster thresholding; figures/tables list peak locations (e.g., VMPFC x=7,y=39,z=-11; right MFG x=32,y=46,z=25; left IFG x=-47,y=24,z=0). A healthy control group is reported separately (n=18). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) that explicitly used cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion (I6) while participants viewed static sad images drawn from IAPS and other normed picture sets (I7). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately alongside an rMDD group (I8). The paper reports task-related contrasts comparing reappraise-sad to attend-sad (i.e., reappraise > attend) in group-level analyses (I9) and provides whole-brain cluster coordinates in tables/figures derived from voxelwise analyses in standard space (MNI/Talairach) (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are violated (e.g., this is not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=17 analyzed) that implemented cognitive reappraisal (distancing) to downregulate emotion to static visual images (IAPS photographs). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise vs. look; repeated-reappraise vs. other conditions) and provides group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space; whole-brain analyses and coordinates (including amygdala and vlPFC peaks) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all review inclusion criteria and violates none.

This study should be excluded because it does not implement reappraisal of static visual images. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (includes a healthy control group), I10 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results with peak coordinates), I11 (results/coordinates clearly described). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reappraisal instruction or regulation task—participants passively viewed sad vs neutral film clips), I7 (stimuli were dynamic film/video clips rather than static visual images), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast such as “reappraise > look”; the reported contrasts reflect emotional reactivity sad > neutral). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults viewing static negative faces (I5, I7, I8 met). However, the task did not instruct participants to perform cognitive reappraisal; the authors infer spontaneous/implicit reappraisal by correlating participants’ face>shape whole-brain maps with an independently derived reappraisal meta-analytic map. The study does not implement an explicit reappraisal regulation task or report a within-task regulation contrast (e.g., “reappraise > look”), so I6 and I9 are not met. Furthermore, the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain task activation map for a reappraisal contrast with peak coordinates in standard space necessary for inclusion (I10 not met). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are directly triggered. Because key inclusion criteria for a reappraisal task-based whole-brain activation contrast are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using static visual images, reporting within-task contrasts and whole-brain coordinates, the emotion-regulation strategy investigated is emotional suppression (instructions to inhibit experience/expression and priming for suppression). The review requires reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, distancing) as the regulation strategy (I6). Because the study does not implement reappraisal, it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using static facial images (I5, I7, I8 satisfied). However, the study did not implement an in-scanner reappraisal emotion-regulation manipulation or provide any within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., “reappraise > look”) — it used passive viewing and assessed reappraisal only via a self-report questionnaire (violates I6 and I9). Analytically, the authors focused on a region-of-interest (ROI) approach (with ROI-controlled inference) rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; although peak coordinates are reported for ROI clusters, no accompanying whole-brain voxelwise map/analysis is provided (violates I10). Because the paper reports only ROI-based task activation results without an accompanying whole-brain map, it meets exclusion criterion E5. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the review and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that used a reappraisal strategy (distancing) delivered socially (psychotherapist) to down-regulate emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Social-Reg > Social-Look) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analysis (cluster-wise FWE correction) and peak coordinates (tables and figures) in standard space. Participants were healthy adult females and results are reported for the target sample. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses an affect labeling task (verbal labeling of facial expressions) rather than an explicit reappraisal instruction (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing). Although the paper describes affect labeling as an incidental form of emotion regulation, it does not implement reappraisal per the review’s definition (I6 not met). The full text otherwise meets multiple inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI; static visual face stimuli; healthy control group reported separately; within-task regulation contrast [affect label vs affect match]; and whole-brain group-level results with reported clusters/coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (reappraisal as the regulation strategy).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key intervention/stimulus criteria for the review. Although it is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that reports within-task regulation contrasts in a healthy elderly control group, the emotion-regulation manipulation is NOT reappraisal: it uses worry induction/suppression via personalized textual worry scripts and prompted imagery of pleasant memories (suppression/distraction), not reinterpretation/distancing/reappraisal of an emotional stimulus. Also, the regulated stimuli are personalized written sentences and imagined memories rather than static visual images (e.g., IAPS pictures or photographs). Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (reappraisal strategy) and I7 (static visual stimuli) are not met. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This study does not use reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing) as the instructed emotion-regulation strategy. Instead, participants were instructed to ‘maintain’ an emotional state (compare or hold emotional responses), which is a maintenance/manipulation task rather than reappraisal. Although the study is task-based fMRI (I5), uses static visual images (I7), includes a healthy adult sample reported separately (I8), reports within-task contrasts (maintain vs non-maintain) and provides whole-brain group results with peak coordinates (I10, I11), it does not implement or report reappraisal-based regulation contrasts (I6) and thus does not meet the review’s core intervention criterion. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered by the full text. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using static visual images (I7) and includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8). It reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps with peak coordinates (I10) and presents coordinate tables/figures (I11). However, the study does not implement reappraisal (reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing with an explicit regulation goal); instead participants performed distraction/working-memory maintenance while viewing negative images, so I6 (use of reappraisal as the regulation strategy) is not met. The paper also does not report any within-task contrast specifically indexing reappraisal versus baseline (e.g., “reappraise > look”), so I9 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and I9.

All inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI with an emotion regulation task using instructed causal attributions (a form of reappraisal/perspective-taking) applied to static visual stimuli (faces). The paper includes a healthy control group reported separately, presents within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., internal>view, external>view, emotion-specific contrasts), and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results with peak MNI coordinates (e.g., left precuneus MNI -6 -55 33) and cluster correction. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

The study is EXCLUDED because the regulated stimuli are autobiographical narrative scripts and flashed text (negative self-beliefs), not static visual images; thus it fails inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal was the regulation strategy), I8 (healthy control group reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported), and I11 (results and coordinates reported in tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are applicable. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude due to violation of I7 (stimulus type).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, voxelwise activation contrasts and coordinate tables; however the regulation targets internally-recalled images (participants recalled previously encoded IAPS pictures from memory while regulating), not externally presented static visual stimuli during scanning. Inclusion criterion I7 requires that the emotional stimuli being regulated are static visual images presented (e.g., IAPS pictures) during the regulation task; it explicitly excludes imagined or recalled scenarios. Therefore the study fails I7 and must be excluded. Study otherwise meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/tables described). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed cognitive reappraisal (down- and up-regulation) as the regulation strategy (I6); stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7); participants were healthy adult volunteers with exclusion of psychiatric/medical disorders and results reported for these healthy groups (I8); the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (downregulate vs look, upregulate vs look) (I9); analyses include whole-brain, voxelwise RFX ANOVA group-level maps with peak coordinates reported in Talairach space (I10), and results/tables describing whole-brain findings are included (I11). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full text meets all review inclusion criteria: it reports a task-based fMRI experiment using cognitive reappraisal (distancing) to down-regulate negative emotion (I5,I6). Stimuli were static visual images (Emotional Picture Set) (I7). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=108) with exclusions and demographics described (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (e.g., RegulateNeg > WatchNeg; WatchNeg > RegulateNeg) (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (RegulateNeg > WatchNeg whole-brain FWE-corrected) and peak coordinates/MNI locations are provided in-text and in supplementary tables (e.g., amygdala and parietal peaks), satisfying the requirement for standard-space coordinates (I10,I11). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced for coordinate lists. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study is excluded because it does not implement a reappraisal emotion-regulation task and does not use static visual images as regulated stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reappraisal/reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing instruction — participants only judged valence), I7 (stimuli are auditory: musical and nonmusical sounds, not static visual images), I9 (no within-task contrast indexing reappraisal vs. baseline/maintain because no regulation instruction was used). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are directly triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly uses cognitive reappraisal as the emotion regulation strategy (I6) with static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample comprises healthy adults screened for psychiatric/medical disorders (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain) and uses these contrasts in second-level analyses (I9). Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported and peak coordinates are provided in standard MNI space (I10), and coordinates/figures/tables are described in the text (I11). Although ROI/SVC analyses were used for some hypotheses, the authors also report whole-brain voxelwise results and provide MNI coordinates for peak activations and connectivity clusters, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain coordinate reporting. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal (distancing) to down-regulate negative emotion using static visual images (IAPS and similar photographs). The sample consists of healthy participants including adults (ages up to 22.9) and results are reported as within-task contrasts (e.g., regulation/negative > reactivity/negative). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses and peak coordinates (amygdala coordinates and other clusters; supplementary tables and tables described), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps in standard space. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5); uses reappraisal as the emotion-regulation strategy (instructing participants to ignore facial expression and rate attractiveness — I6); regulated stimuli are static visual images (KDEF photos of faces — I7); sample consists of healthy adults (n=18) with no reported disorders (I8); reports within-task contrast comparing high-control (reappraise) > low-control (rate) for the emotion domain (I9); and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using cognitive reappraisal (including distancing/perspective-taking) to up- and down-regulate negative emotion (I6). Stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample comprises healthy adult participants with results reported for the healthy group (I8). The manuscript reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., increase > look, decrease > look) (I9) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in standard (MNI/ICBM) space and tables of coordinates (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are met. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implemented reappraisal via the distancing strategy while participants viewed static IAPS images of social (interpersonal) scenes. The design crossed instruction (distance vs. look) with stimulus valence (negative vs. neutral) and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., distance > look, look > distance) for the healthy control group. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM2) with cluster-correction and results reported with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a detachment (distancing/perspective-taking) strategy to intentionally downregulate emotion in response to static IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task regulation versus permit (no-regulation) contrasts, group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with FWE correction) and peak coordinates for amygdala and other activations (standard space). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults directly testing reappraisal strategies (Reinterpretation and Detachment) using static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’ and reverse) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates (MNI), and presents results in main text/tables. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm (Suppress vs Maintain) with static IAPS images. The sample includes a healthy control group (non-drug-using controls) and the paper reports the relevant within-task contrasts (Maintain>Observe and Suppress>Maintain). The authors performed group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (in addition to ROI/SVC tests) with cluster-level correction and indicate that detailed one-sample task activations and between-group whole-brain comparisons (with coordinates) are provided in Supplementary Tables S1–S7. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 (and I11). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply.

This article reports a task-based fMRI study in which participants were trained to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion (Reduce vs Maintain), using static IAPS images as stimuli. The sample includes a healthy control group (Normal Anxiety; no history of mood/anxiety disorders). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (AlphaSim correction) and significant clusters from the Reduce>Maintain contrast and group contrasts are reported in tables/figures, indicating peak coordinates in standard space. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based reappraisal with static visual stimuli in healthy adults and provides whole-brain coordinate results.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used reappraisal strategies (increase by engaging; decrease by distancing) to regulate emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS threat-related pictures). The sample comprised healthy adult participants (n=24, females) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (increase > view, decrease > view, view > decrease) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and figures). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text reviewed and is complete. This study is excluded because the emotion-regulation strategy examined is distraction (memorize vs. view), not reappraisal (reinterpretation, distancing, or perspective-taking). While the paper is a task-based fMRI study using static visual images, includes a healthy control group, and reports whole-brain peak coordinates, it does not implement or report a reappraisal-based regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look) for the healthy adults. Therefore it fails the critical inclusion criteria I6 (reappraisal strategy) and I9 (within-task reappraisal contrast). No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal (positive reappraisal) to downregulate emotional responses to static IAPS images. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., [view NEG – reappraise]) and random-effects group analyses. Although primary ROI/SVC analyses are emphasized, the paper states complementary exploratory whole-brain analyses are provided in the supplementary material (Supplementary Table 1) and reports peak voxel locations for contrasts, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task activation maps with coordinates. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) This is a task-based fMRI study; (I6) Explicit reappraisal instructions (MAINTAIN/INCREASE/DECREASE) implemented as reinterpretation/distancing strategies; (I7) Emotional stimuli are static visual images (IAPS photographs and similar pictures); (I8) Includes a healthy adult control group (n=15) with results reported separately and compared to patients; (I9) Reports within-task regulation contrasts (DECREASE > MAINTAIN; INCREASE > MAINTAIN) and related analyses; (I10) Presents group-level, whole-brain task activation results with peak coordinates reported in MNI space (tables and text; Supplement noted for within-group contrasts); (I11) Whole-brain results and coordinates are provided in the main text/tables and referenced supplementary material. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focusing on reappraisal of static visual stimuli in healthy adults.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation using cognitive reappraisal of static visual food images with whole-brain group-level contrasts and coordinates (meets I5, I6, I7, I9, I10, I11). However, the sample is a developmental cohort of females aged 10–23 and the analyses are reported across the full mixed-age sample; no separate group-level results restricted to a healthy adult-only group are reported. The meta-analysis requires at least one group of healthy adults with results reported separately (I8), which is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, task-based simultaneous EEG-fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults using static visual IAPS images (meeting I5–I8) and it reports within-task comparisons related to reappraisal (I9), the fMRI results are reported at the AAL ROI level (mean ROI Z-scores) and via KCCA/GLM summaries rather than as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in a standard space. No MNI/Talairach peak coordinates or whole-brain voxelwise maps are provided. Therefore it fails I10 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal in healthy adults using static visual images and reports within-task contrasts, it does not report group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps with peak coordinates. Analyses rely on ROI-based amygdala activation and PPI connectivity restricted to IFG masks; whole-brain task-evoked coordinates for the reappraisal contrast are not provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI/restricted analyses without accompanying whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used), I7 (static visual image stimuli), I8 (healthy adult control group reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrast reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (group-level whole-brain task activation map with peak coordinates). Full text appears complete.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (26 women) that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to decrease negative affect (reappraise vs look). The regulation was applied while viewing static visual face stimuli (neutral faces presented during the instruction period), fulfilling the stimulus requirement. The paper reports within-task contrasts relating to regulation (e.g., reappraise > look) and performs whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and reports coordinates/tables and figures. The sample excludes psychiatric/neurological disorders and presents group-level whole-brain results for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not investigate reappraisal-based emotion regulation. Participants performed an attentional spatial-cueing task and were instructed to ignore emotional face distracters rather than to reappraise, so I6 (reappraisal used) is not met. The paper does not report any within-task reappraisal vs control contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look), so I9 (within-task regulation contrast) is not met. Analyses focus on ACC and PFC using anatomical masks and small-volume correction rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map, so it fails I10 and meets exclusion E5 (ROI/SVC-only results without whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (regulated stimuli are static visual images—faces), I8 (healthy adult sample), and I11 (peak coordinates are reported for reported activations). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria met: E5. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion are present). Thus the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study meets several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that explicitly implemented reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy (I6) while participants viewed static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately and within-group analyses (I8), and the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise vs. view; I9). However, the fMRI analyses were conducted using anatomically defined ROIs (AAL masks) and activations were examined/thresholded within these ROIs (methods state that ROIs were used for all analyses). There is no clear indication of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported (I10 not met). Because results appear to be ROI-restricted (or small-volume corrected) without accompanying whole-brain maps, this triggers exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus the study is excluded for failing I10 and meeting E5.

This study must be excluded because the regulated stimuli are personalized worry sentences (textual/narrative scripts) presented on-screen, not static visual images such as IAPS photographs (fails I7). Although the study is task-based neuroimaging (I5), implements reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy (I6), includes a healthy older adult control group reported separately (I8), and reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (reappraisal vs rest) (I9), the stimulus modality requirement is not met. Additionally, the provided full text does not contain explicit whole-brain peak coordinates in standard space so I10 cannot be verified from the supplied content. Therefore it does not satisfy all inclusion criteria.

Full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual images used), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., PosUp > PosWatch), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates in MNI space reported), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Did NOT meet I6: the task instructed participants to ‘up-regulate’ affect but explicitly stated that no specific emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, reinterpretation, perspective-taking, distancing) was instructed; therefore the study does not implement reappraisal (broadly construed) as the controlled strategy required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to failure to meet I6 (reappraisal requirement).

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (API error in provided full text), preventing verification of methods and results. Based on title/metadata this appears to be an fMRI study of lorazepam effects in catatonia rather than a reappraisal task in healthy adults. Exclusion IDs met: none (E4- E8 not confirmed). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met / could not be confirmed: I5 (task details not confirmed), I6 (no evidence reappraisal was used), I7 (stimulus type not confirmed as static visual images), I8 (target sample likely clinical rather than healthy adults or healthy controls not reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrast not confirmed), I10 (whole-brain coordinates not reported/confirmed). fulltext_incomplete=true; cannot include without complete article confirming criteria.

This fMRI study is task-based (I5), uses static visual images as stimuli (I7), includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8), and reports within-task contrasts comparing strategies (evaluation vs distraction), i.e., a regulation contrast (distraction > evaluation / evaluation > distraction) (I9). However, the emotion regulation strategy tested is attentional distraction (bar-orientation task), not reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing), so it fails inclusion criterion I6. In addition, the provided full text does not report whole-brain peak coordinates in a standard space (Talairach/MNI) for the regulation contrasts (I10 not met).
